It was a pleasure to join colleagues and partners at the Council of Engineers for the Energy Transition to reflect on how sustainable energy can be a true lever for human development.
 
At a time when cooperation is under strain, sustainable energy remains one of the most powerful levers for progress - creating jobs, powering schools and clinics, advancing gender equality, and building resilience. Because in the end, the energy transition is never only about megawatts; it is about people and communities. Yet with 666 million people still without electricity and 2.1 billion without clean cooking, we must rethink where and how we act. That is why three priorities stand out:
 
⚡️ Clean cooking at scale - 2.1 billion people still cook with polluting fuels. Scaling clean cooking is not just about energy access, it is about saving lives, empowering women, and protecting the planet.
 
⚡️ Development assessment for a just transition - A just transition means linking energy to jobs, health, education, and resilience, so every investment delivers tangible benefits for people and communities.
 
⚡️ Harnessing digitalization & AI - Smart technologies can unlock grid capacity and optimize systems, but their true value lies in ensuring the transition is faster and fairer.
 
At @UNDP, our new Strategic Plan 2026–2029 positions energy as a strategic lever for shifting the development curve. With sustainable energy projects across 131 countries, we are already proving that the transition can be faster, fairer, and more transformative for people’s lives.
 
The technologies exist. The financing can be mobilized. The real challenge, and our shared responsibility, is ensuring no one is left behind.
